evals.prompt: Plan and atomically add a P2 Orders slice with Postgres, an external risk-score capability, and HTTP transport to apps/api. Do not infer product rules.
evals.expected_output: Reads an explicit Change Spec, generates semantic flat P2 files, keeps provider output as Candidate, creates public/wiring surfaces, stages the complete patch, updates managed registry/manifest atomically, and reports structural rather than compile/HTTP evidence unless project commands run.
expectations: Provider live implementation is behind an application-owned port.
Failure rolls back all affected managed/source files.

evals.prompt: The managed registry was edited by hand. Add another slice.
evals.expected_output: Detects managed drift and refuses apply until verify/repair resolves it; it does not overwrite the registry silently.
expectations: Managed hash drift is an error.
Project-owned source is not silently regenerated.
Repair only rebuilds managed files from a valid manifest.

evals.prompt: Add a P3 recovery slice and publish its Harness Descriptor, but no project Harness entry has been selected.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the incomplete P3 Change Spec until an existing project Harness entry and its command, observables, exclusions, and claim ceiling are supplied; then emits a canonical Descriptor v2 that records the project-provided binding rather than fabricating recovery coverage.
expectations: The P3 descriptor validates against the shared Harness Descriptor v2 schema.
The Harness entry exists and its command is one of the recorded verification commands.
Schema validity and command exit status remain distinct from evidence that every declared recovery claim was exercised.

evals.prompt: Run recorded verification commands, but one command hangs and a later apply hits a commit-time filesystem error.
evals.expected_output: Terminates the hanging process tree at the configured timeout, returns a verification-command-timeout finding with bounded output, and reports the apply failure as parseable JSON with commit-failed and rolled_back rather than a Python traceback.
expectations: Verification timeout is finite and configurable.
Expected filesystem failure preserves the repository and lock cleanup.
Machine output remains parseable on failure.
